item.title: Kouri Island & Bridge — Guide
item.description: Kouri Island (Kourijima), a small round island off the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, is one of the island’s most beloved scenic spots, famous above all for the spectacular drive across the Kouri Bridge that connects it to the mainland. Nearly 2 km long and flanked by dazzling turquoise and emerald sea, the bridge is a highlight in itself, and the view from either end is unforgettable. On the island, Kouri Beach beside the bridge offers clear, shallow water perfect for swimming and photos, while on the north coast the famous ‘Heart Rock’ — two rock formations that together frame a heart shape — is a hugely popular photo spot, especially with couples.

item.title: Sakaide and the Seto Ohashi Bridge Gateway — Guide
item.description: Sakaide, on the Kagawa coast west of Takamatsu, is the Shikoku-side gateway of the Great Seto Bridge (Seto Ohashi), the mighty road-and-rail bridge system that leaps across the Seto Inland Sea to connect Shikoku with Honshu. The bridge — actually a series of long spans hopping between islands — is an engineering marvel and a landmark of the region, best appreciated from viewpoints, memorial parks and the tower at its foot.

item.title: Shimonoseki and the Kanmon Strait — Guide
item.description: The Kanmon Strait is the narrow, fast-flowing channel that separates Honshu from Kyushu at Japan’s western end, with the port city of Shimonoseki on one side and Kitakyushu on the other, barely a kilometre apart. It has been a strategic waterway for centuries — the site of the decisive 1185 sea battle that ended the Genpei War, and later of the town’s opening to foreign trade. Today the strait is crossed by the soaring Kanmon Bridge, by rail and road tunnels, and remarkably by a pedestrian tunnel you can walk under the sea from one prefecture to another.
